newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF not mulling steps to deal with yen - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF not mulling steps to deal with yen - Jiji.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday that he is not at the moment considering special measures to deal with the weakness of the yen, Jiji news agency reported.
He also reiterated that excessive weakness or strength of the yen was undesirable, Jiji said.
"Generally speaking, I would like to say that we will deal appropriately (with excessive currency moves)," Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying.
"We are calmly watching the market at the moment and are not specially considering (measures) for now," he said.
He added wild moves in the foreign exchange market were not desirable.
"A stable foreign exchange market would help us promote credibility and steady economic growth," Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying.
Mitsuzuka said he hoped the currency market would settle down by the time finance ministers and central bankers from the Group of Seven (G7) nations meet on February 8.
